response:
## VERDICT

**HOLD.**

Not because the mechanism is wrong in principle, but because as specified it cannot fail. Every arm of the current design produces a plausible-looking result, and none of them distinguish "persistent internal dynamics causally alter the agents" from "the reflect prompt got longer and reordered." Two weeks of runs would yield a graph nobody can interpret. Hold until the confound below is designed out — which is a few days of harness work, not a redesign.

---

## HIDDEN ASSUMPTION

**The workspace is called endogenous, but no state variable in it has dynamics of its own.**

Walk the terms: importance is assigned at write time from the observation. Recency is a clock function of the observation stream. Slow strength is an exponentially-weighted sum of past activations, which are themselves functions of observations. Source bias is a constant. There is no feedback from ignition back into the trace dynamics — no refractory period, no depletion, no inhibition of competitors, no self-generated drive.

That means the entire workspace is a **causal function of the observation history**. It is a low-pass filter with a comparator on the output. Two instances given identical input tapes will produce identical workspace states forever. "Spontaneous endogenous activity" is on your motivating list and is precisely the property the implementation lacks. What you have built is a re-ranker with hysteresis, which is a respectable thing to build, but it is not a workspace and it will not produce divergence over time.

The assumption stays hidden because of a second design choice that hides it: **ignition is additive.** EW-on prepends broadcast text to the reflect prompt; EW-off does not. So EW-on strictly increases the information and token count going into the LLM. Any improvement you measure is confounded with "more context, differently ordered." That confound will generate a positive result whether or not the mechanism is real, and it is the single most likely way this project produces a false success.

Secondary, and worth naming because it violates one of your own constraints: the workspace generates no prose, but **reflect does**, and reflect's output is written back to memory. Ignition therefore launders re-broadcast old content into new memory objects with new timestamps. Run this long enough and you get autobiographical drift through a channel you have declared closed. It is not the workspace inventing facts. It is the workspace deciding which facts get re-narrated until the narration becomes the record.

---

## UNCONVENTIONAL MOVE

**Make the workspace subtractive and zero-sum, and move ignition from the read side to the write side.**

Concretely, two coupled changes that constitute one mechanism — call it **scarcity consolidation**:

1. **Hard capacity, not a threshold.** Reflect receives exactly K slots (K ≈ 3–5), always, in every condition. EW-off fills them with top-K retrieval score. EW-on fills them with ignition winners. Ignition no longer adds anything; it *reallocates*. Now the two arms are token-matched and information-quantity-matched, and the only difference is *which* items win. That is the variable you actually care about, and it is currently unmeasurable.

2. **Ignition gates consolidation, not access.** Only ignited items receive a persistence credit in long-term memory — their retrieval strength is refreshed, their decay slows, non-ignited items decay normally. Add a global consumable: each ignition draws from a budget that recovers on a slow time constant, so ignition history feeds back into ignition eligibility. This is the missing feedback loop, and it is what gives the system a state variable that is *not* a function of the input alone.

Why this teaches more than tuning weights: read-gating can only change what an agent says this turn. Write-gating changes **which parts of an agent's history survive**, which is the only route by which two agents on similar input tapes can develop genuinely different memory stores. That is your stated goal — developmental selection, multiple timescales — and it is measurable in a numeric memory-store distance metric, not in dialogue vibes. It also makes the mechanism *worse* at looking brain-like, which is a point in its favor.

While you are in there: LLM-rated "importance" is not a measurement, it is a text-style correlate. It scores dramatic-sounding memories highly. Slow traces integrate that bias for the entire run. Consider replacing or supplementing it with a self-prediction error signal — how badly the agent's own retrieval-based next-state prediction missed — which is falsifiable, cheap, and not a function of prose register.

---

## ABLATION

Three arms, one fixed observation tape, seeded generation, K held constant everywhere:

- **A — Capacity-matched off.** K slots, filled by retrieval score.
- **B — EW on.** K slots, filled by ignition winners, consolidation credit applied.
- **C — Yoked shuffle.** The critical arm. Replay B's exact ignition *timing and count*, but permute *which* items occupy the slots (sample from the same candidate pool, matched on importance and recency distribution). Consolidation credit applied to the shuffled winners.

C is the falsifier. It preserves every structural property of the mechanism — perturbation rate, timing statistics, capacity pressure, write-gating — and destroys only the claim that ignition selects *the right content*.

Primary dependent variable must be non-linguistic. Suggested: memory-store divergence between twin agents over time (Jaccard or embedding-centroid distance on surviving high-strength memories), plus behavioral divergence on a held-out probe set of decision points. Judged dialogue quality is a secondary measure at best and should not be pre-registered as primary.

Minimum useful N: run each arm across ~8–10 tape seeds. Single-run differences here are noise.

---

## FAILURE SIGNATURE

The mechanism is decorative if any of these hold:

- **B ≈ C.** Ignition content doesn't matter; only the perturbation does. This is the most likely outcome and you should expect it.
- **Divergence is a contraction.** Twin agents' memory stores diverge under perturbation, then reconverge. If the workspace pulls trajectories back toward a common attractor, the persistent state is a filter, not a memory.
- **Ignition rank correlates >0.9 with retrieval rank.** The threshold is relabeling. Check this in the first hour of logs; if it is true, stop.
- **Advantage disappears under capacity matching.** If B beat the *uncapped* off condition but ties A, the whole effect was prompt length.
- **Slow-trace ablation is null.** Set the decay time constant to 0 and to ∞. If neither extreme changes the dependent variable beyond noise, the second timescale is doing nothing.
- **Anything improves and nobody can say which item ignited.** If the causal chain from a specific ID to a specific behavioral change cannot be traced in logs, the claim is unfalsifiable regardless of the number.

---

## ONE CHANGE BEFORE START

**Build the deterministic record-and-replay harness before anything else, with the yoked-shuffle arm as a first-class citizen rather than an afterthought.**

Specifically: a frozen observation tape, seeded LLM sampling with temperature and seed logged per call, full workspace state dumped every tick (all candidate IDs, scores, trace values, budget level, ignition events with timestamps), and provenance tags propagated from broadcast IDs through reflect outputs into any resulting memory writes. The harness must be able to take run B's ignition schedule as *input* and produce run C from it.

Without this, EW-on and EW-off are not comparable, C cannot be constructed at all, and the autobiographical-laundering path is invisible. With it, every ablation above becomes a config flag rather than a rebuild — and you get the drift audit for free.

One more thing worth deciding before you start rather than after: pre-register the primary metric and the effect size you would accept. This design has enough free parameters that a motivated analyst will find a positive result in it. That is the real risk here, more than any bug in the scoring function.
